az_phoenix_areas.blurb: Climbing around greater Phoenix and Scottsdale is spread across city parks, desert mountains and small urban crags. Bouldering is the biggest part, followed by traditional lines, with a smaller helping of sport routes and a few aid and top-rope lines. Roped grades cluster from 5.9 to 5.11, with moderates below and a thin tail into the 5.12s, while boulder problems run from easy up through the V8 range and a handful harder. South Mountain is the main bouldering hub on granite, while the McDowell Mountains and Pinnacle Peak hold granite trad with cracks and precise face climbing. Camelback Mountain mixes sport and trad, and the Superstition Mountains and Little Granite Mountain add more remote options. Winter is the prime season, since summers are long and hot.

ca_yosemite_valley.blurb: Yosemite Valley is the heart of Yosemite National Park, a setting of mild weather, big scenery and sheer granite walls that make it one of the best-known climbing arenas anywhere. Traditional climbing leads by a wide margin, with a large bouldering scene, a modest amount of sport climbing and some aid. Roped grades run from 5.6 through the mid-5.12s and beyond, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.12 and the busiest band around 5.10 and 5.11; boulder problems range from easy to V12 and up. The cliffs divide into Valley North Side, Valley South Side and Yosemite Valley Bouldering, and the Lower Merced River Canyon adds more.

id_east_idaho.blurb: East Idaho covers the Snake River Plain country around American Falls and Pocatello, with more crags scattered toward the Teton side of the state. The cliffs are volcanic basalt, steep and often overhanging, with edges, pockets, roofs and some cracks. Sport climbing dominates by a large margin, with a strong bouldering scene and a smaller number of trad and top-rope lines. Roped grades are concentrated from 5.10 through 5.12, so strong intermediates and up are well served, with fewer easy routes below 5.9. Massacre Rocks and Teddy Bear Cove, a few miles apart, hold the most climbs, with Pocatello bouldering, Ross Park and the Teton River canyon adding variety. Late fall and early spring are best, sunny winter days stay climbable in sheltered alcoves, and summer is very hot.

ca_central_joshua_tree.blurb: Central Joshua Tree sits in the middle of Joshua Tree National Park in the high desert, approached from the town of Joshua Tree to the north or from Twentynine Palms and the Cottonwood side to the east. It is mostly traditional climbing on rock formations scattered across sandy flats, with plenty of boulders, a good number of top-rope lines and a few sport routes. Grades are friendly: a broad spread of moderates, with the busiest band from 5.8 to 5.10 and a modest number of harder 5.11 and 5.12 lines. The main clusters are Sheep Pass, Echo Rock and Barker Dam, with the Comic Book area and Stonehenge boulders as extras. Winter, spring and fall are the comfortable seasons. Approach trails can be deep sand, and many walk-offs are steep.

ca_western_sierra.blurb: The Western Sierra gathers many scattered crags on the western slope of the Sierra Nevada. Traditional climbing leads, with a big share of sport routes, a fair amount of bouldering and a few alpine lines. Grades mostly run from 5.7 to 5.12, with the busiest band around 5.10, so there is something for most levels. At Shuteye Ridge and Courtright Reservoir the rock is granite, with knobs, edges, friction slabs and cracks, and approaches are often long. Courtright suits late spring to late fall, while Shuteye is best in fall and spring. The Needles and Kern River area adds a high concentration of trad lines in Sequoia National Forest.

vt_1_northern_vermont.blurb: Northern Vermont stretches from the Burlington area to the Northeast Kingdom, and it offers rock, boulders and ice. Bouldering is the largest part, followed by trad and sport routes, with a real ice scene and a few mixed lines. Roped grades are wide-ranging but centre on 5.9 to 5.12, while boulder problems run from V0 into the double digits, and ice is mostly WI3 to WI5. Bolton is the biggest hub, on schist that ranges from solid to loose, with sport crags, trad buttresses and many boulders. Smugglers' Notch adds multi-pitch routes, cliffs, ice and technical boulders, and Groton and Black Mountain add more. Climbing near Burlington stays reliable into early November, while the Northeast Kingdom turns too cold by then.
